extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / international affairs readers
extracted.subtask_description: Write datelined newspaper dispatches reporting foreign/diplomatic and military events, summarizing official statements, public reaction, historical background, and international ramifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution ('Reliable sources said')
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear attribution when reporting non-official information (e.g., "Reliable sources said Lithuania had been told bluntly by Germany...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag unconfirmed reports with phrases like "Reliable sources said" or "There were reports" to indicate sourcing and caution; include variations such as "It was understood" when relaying diplomatic leaks or unofficial accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: News agency dateline and byline
rubrics_metrics.description: Include dateline/agency attribution for dispatches (examples: "By The Associated Press" and place-and-date lines such as "KAUNAS, Lithuania, March 23").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the dispatch-byline format to show origin of report and establish timeliness and provenance of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and legal background (Treaty context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide historical/legal context for territorial events (e.g., reference to the Treaty of Versailles: "Hitler feels entitled because the World War peacemakers took it away from Germany—under the Treaty of Versailles of June 28, 1919").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize prior status, key legal instruments, dates and prior transfers to help readers understand the significance of current events; include population and territorial statistics when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official statements and government proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Report official government remarks and parliamentary debate (examples: "Sir Samuel said... told the House of Commons"; "The Government reported that Germany had threatened little Lithuania...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote officials directly where possible; summarize cabinet decisions, replies in legislatures and formal government communications to convey policy positions and official responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military movements and mobilization details
rubrics_metrics.description: Document military preparations and troop movements (e.g., "national military reserves were called", "reservists called under Premier Daladier’s new dictatorial powers", "troops massed on the Rumanian border").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify calls-up, deployment locations, mobilization orders and changes in readiness; indicate sources and any verification limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reaction, demonstrations and civil unrest
rubrics_metrics.description: Record popular responses and street-level events (examples: "The German population, 72 per cent of the total, greeted news of Anschluss with rejoicing"; "Socialists held anti-demonstrations...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe demonstrations, chants, holidays, protective police measures and public sentiment to convey social impact and atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local occupation and symbolic actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report concrete acts of takeover and symbolism at the local level (e.g., "Trucks and freight cars loaded with the possessions of refugees were halted... The customs house and postoffices were occupied. The Memel radio station immediately started broadcasting German military marches. Swastikas appeared everywhere").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of administrative, communications and customs seizures and visible symbols to illustrate the nature and character of an occupation or transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and diplomatic consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover economic measures and diplomatic accords linked to the event (examples: "The German economics ministry... studying the 25 per cent extra duties imposed by the United States"; "Rumania and Germany concluded a 'normal' trade agreement").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report trade treaties, sanctions, tariff changes, credits and economic negotiations as part of the broader international implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refugees and humanitarian impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight civilian dislocation and humanitarian effects (examples: "Trucks and freight cars loaded with the possessions of refugees were halted"; "flight of Jews from the territory").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail interruptions to refugee movements, confiscation or halting of possessions, arrests, and other civilian hardships arising from the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronology, dates and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide precise dates and sequence of events (numerous date references such as "March 22", "May 8, 1924", and event timelines throughout the dispatches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use datelines and dated references to establish a clear timeline and to make the report timely and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple international perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reactions and positions from several countries and actors (coverage spans Britain, France, Poland, Rumania, Denmark, Hungary, Italy and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the viewpoints, policy moves and domestic reactions of all relevant states and international organizations to give readers a comprehensive understanding of diplomatic fallout.
